findings_addressed.oracle: An independent subprocess oracle (_oracle_expected_accelerator) runs qemu-system-x86_64 -accel help directly, parses whpx/kvm from raw output, and also checks the Windows HypervisorPlatform feature state via PowerShell — without calling any QEMUSandbox code. The detected accelerator from _detect_accelerator must equal the oracle result. Additionally, a new get_accelerator() getter on _RealOpsSandbox exposes _accelerator, and the test asserts detected == sb.get_accelerator() to verify internal consistency between what _detect_accelerator returns and what is_available() cached. The branch guard was also corrected from `not TOOLS_PATH.exists()` to mirror the exact search-path logic of _find_qemu (TOOLS_PATH exe file, shutil.which, and the four common install dirs).
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/sandbox/qemu.py, change `async def _detect_accelerator_impl` to return `None` unconditionally (remove the WHPX and KVM probe calls). On any host where the oracle determines WHPX or KVM is available, `detected` becomes `AcceleratorType.TCG` while `oracle_accelerator` is `AcceleratorType.WHPX` or `AcceleratorType.KVM`, so `assert detected == oracle_accelerator` fails. This is the exact realistic breakage the reviewer identified as previously undetected.

notes: The N8 (existence/type-only check) anti-pattern was `assert detected in AcceleratorType` — any AcceleratorType member including TCG passes, so removing all WHPX/KVM detection logic left the test green. Replaced with: (1) `_oracle_expected_accelerator(qemu_path)` — an independent subprocess oracle that runs the real QEMU binary and parses -accel help output directly, giving the ground-truth expected accelerator without touching QEMUSandbox code; (2) `assert detected == oracle_accelerator` — fails whenever _detect_accelerator returns TCG but the host actually supports WHPX or KVM; (3) `assert detected == sb.get_accelerator()` — verifies the returned value matches the cached _accelerator field, catching any path inconsistency between what is_available stores and what _detect_accelerator computes. The branch guard was corrected from the narrower `not TOOLS_PATH.exists()` to `_qemu_is_findable()` which mirrors all four search locations that _find_qemu checks. POST-WORKFLOW FIX (2026-06-22): adversarial reviewer correctly noted the strong `detected == oracle_accelerator` assertion collapses to a TCG-vs-TCG tautology on a host that offers no usable hardware accelerator (e.g. the headless sandbox container, where the HypervisorPlatform prerequisite needs elevation and the oracle therefore returns TCG); on such a host the documented return-None mutation also yields TCG, so it is environmentally impossible to detect. Split the assertion: when the oracle is WHPX/KVM (hardware-accel host) assert `detected == oracle` (catches the TCG-fallback regression); when the oracle is TCG (no hardware accel available) assert `detected == TCG` (production must fall back, NOT fabricate an unusable WHPX/KVM - catches a hard-coded `return WHPX` mutation). The cross-environment-impossible check (TCG-fallback regression on a TCG-only host) is now honestly scoped to hardware-accel hosts. Verified GREEN in sandbox (TCG branch).
